patterns.name: Row of cards
patterns.structure: One row of equal cards, each with a numbered marker, a heading and a paragraph.
content_fit: a set of items of the same kind, listed side by side
features, services, arguments, options - anything that reads as a list
not for items that follow one another in time, use a process pattern

cards.note: at 14pt a fourth card drops the line to about 26 characters

variants: drop the number marker
two rows for up to 6 items
cards without a heading -> plain text columns

patterns.name: Row of cards, room size
patterns.structure: Three cards at presentation size: 40pt title, 24pt headings, 20pt body.
content_fit: the card row for a slide shown on a wall rather than a screen
three points is the most that stays readable at this size
the text per card is roughly half of the screen version

cards.note: a fourth card does not stay readable at 20pt

variants: two cards for a comparison

patterns.name: Path with milestones
patterns.structure: A horizontal line with numbered stations; each label sits above or below, alternating.
content_fit: steps that follow one another in time
a roadmap, a procedure, a history
the alternating labels are what let a step carry a real sentence

stations.note: at 14pt six stations leave about 22 characters a line

variants: all labels above -> a plain timeline
square markers instead of round
a date line under each station
patterns.carrier: the line the stations sit on

patterns.name: Chevron stages
patterns.structure: Interlocking chevrons carrying a stage number, with the caption alternating above and below.
content_fit: a sequence where each stage hands over to the next
a pipeline, an approval chain, a customer journey
reads as strictly ordered - not for a set of equal items
variants: captions all below -> more room per caption
the last chevron as a plain arrow head -> emphasises the outcome

patterns.name: Cards in two rows, read back and forth
patterns.structure: Two rows of cards; numbering runs left to right on top and right to left below, so the two rows read as one chain.
content_fit: six steps that do not fit in one row
a process with two halves - preparation and execution, before and after
the numbering carries the order, so the cards themselves stay equal
variants: numbering left to right in both rows -> two groups instead of one chain
numbering left to right in both rows -> two groups
patterns.carrier: the two rows read in order

patterns.name: Staircase of steps
patterns.structure: Overlapping blocks climbing from bottom left to top right, each with a marker above it and a darkening tone.
content_fit: stages that build on each other and get bigger, later or more advanced
years, maturity levels, a growth path
the climb says progress - not for equal options

steps.note: at 14pt five is the limit before the blocks swallow each other

variants: descending instead -> a decline
even tones -> the climb alone carries it

patterns.name: Hub with satellites
patterns.structure: A centre shape with three labels to its left and three to its right, each joined by a line.
content_fit: one thing and the parts that feed into it
a platform and its channels, a role and its duties, a product and its benefits
everything points at the centre - not for a sequence

satellites.note: always even, three a side at six

variants: all satellites on one side -> a legend layout
drop the lines

patterns.name: Pyramid of levels
patterns.structure: Stacked bars widening downward, each level named inside and explained in a column to the left.
content_fit: levels that build on one another - a maturity model, a hierarchy of needs
the width says how much of something a level holds
not for equal parts of a whole, that is a bar or a pie
variants: upside down -> a funnel
labels on both sides
equal widths -> a plain stack

patterns.name: Funnel with a list on each side
patterns.structure: Stages narrowing downward, with a column of notes to the left and to the right, each line aligned to its stage.
content_fit: something that loses volume at every step
two readings of the same steps - what happens, and what it means
one column alone works too, then the stages sit off-centre
variants: no side lists -> a plain funnel
turned over -> a pyramid

patterns.name: Matrix with named axes
patterns.structure: A grid of cells with a heading over each column and a label block beside each row.
content_fit: two dimensions crossed - effort against value, performance against potential
each cell carries a name and a line saying what it means
the cell tone is a third reading and can be dropped
variants: 2x2 -> the classic four-quadrant picture
one tone for all cells

patterns.name: Four quadrants
patterns.structure: Two axes and four quadrants, each a card with a name and a line saying what belongs there.
content_fit: two yes/no dimensions crossed - urgent against important, effort against value
each quadrant needs a name, otherwise it is four boxes
the tone can say which quadrant you want to be in
variants: no tones -> position alone carries it
markers plotted inside a quadrant

patterns.name: Wall of key figures
patterns.structure: Equal panels, each with one large figure, a short label and a line of context.
content_fit: measured results - counts, shares, durations, money
one figure per panel, never two
the context line is what stops a number from standing unexplained
variants: drop the context line -> a tighter band above other content
one panel in a darker tone -> the figure that matters most

patterns.name: Two columns compared row by row
patterns.structure: Two headed columns with a row label to the left; every row states the same question for both sides.
content_fit: two options weighed against each other on the same criteria
before and after, us and them, plan and result
the row label is the criterion, so it stays short
variants: three columns -> narrower cells
one column in a darker tone -> which side wins

patterns.name: Media on one side, text on the other
patterns.structure: A picture area filling about half the width, with a heading, a paragraph and three bullet lines beside it.
content_fit: anything that has a picture - a product, a place, a person, a screenshot
the bullets carry the three things worth saying about it
the picture area stays a grey block until a real image is dropped in
variants: picture on the right -> mirrored
no bullets -> one long paragraph
two stacked picture areas -> before and after

patterns.name: One statement
patterns.structure: A single large sentence in the middle of the slide with one line of attribution or context under it.
content_fit: the one thing the audience should remember
a quotation, a claim, a decision, a result
it works because nothing else is on the slide - do not add a second point
variants: drop the context line
a figure above the sentence

patterns.name: Agenda with a key column
patterns.structure: A time or number block on the left, a vertical spine with a marker per entry, and a wide block per entry on the right.
content_fit: an agenda, a schedule, a plan with times
any list where each item has a short key and a description
the left block need not be a time - a phase, a number, a name all work

entries.note: at 14pt a fourth entry leaves the block too short for a heading and a line

variants: two blocks per row -> morning and afternoon side by side
drop the spine -> a plain two-column list

patterns.name: Text in two columns
patterns.structure: A lead paragraph across the full width, then two columns of running text, each with a small heading.
content_fit: a slide that has to carry real prose - a position, an explanation, a summary
the lead is the claim, the columns are the argument
for a handout or a shared screen, never for a wall
variants: three columns -> shorter lines
drop the lead

patterns.name: Status table with timeline bars
patterns.structure: Header chips over a table body; one narrow column carries a state marker, the right block is a time grid with one bar per row; legend below.
content_fit: a list of items each with an owner, a state and a duration
projects, measures, packages of work - anything tracked over a period
not for a plain list without a second dimension, use a card row

body_rows.note: at 14pt six rows is the limit before the table fills the slide

time_columns.note: 0 turns it into a plain status table

variants: drop the time block -> comparison table
drop the state column -> plain data table
bars all full width -> presence matrix instead of durations

patterns.name: Chart with callout cards
patterns.structure: A real chart object in the middle with a card each side, joined by a short rule.
content_fit: a split of one whole into parts, where each part needs a sentence
shares of revenue, of effort, of an audience
the chart is a live chart object with its own data, not a picture

segments.note: beyond four use a legend instead of cards

variants: bar chart -> more segments possible
legend below instead of cards

patterns.name: Bar chart with readings
patterns.structure: A live clustered-column chart filling two thirds of the slide, with cards beside it saying what to read out of it.
content_fit: measured values across categories, two series compared
the cards are the point - a chart without a reading is decoration
works for one series too, then the legend goes
variants: line chart -> a trend rather than a comparison
horizontal bars -> long category names fit
cards below instead of beside -> a wider chart

patterns.name: Chain across two zones
patterns.structure: Two bounded zones side by side, each holding a short chain of steps, with a marked boundary between them, a row of chips below and one full-width closing bar.
content_fit: a process that crosses a border - two companies, two systems, two countries
the point is that it is one chain, not two separate ones
the chips below are what holds true across both zones
variants: drop the closing bar
three zones -> narrower chains
no chips row

patterns.name: Cards carrying a list
patterns.structure: Equal cards, each with a heading and four bullet lines, alternating light and dark.
content_fit: a set of areas, each with the things it contains
a portfolio, a service catalogue, four teams and their duties
the bullets are labels, not sentences - one line each
variants: all cards the same tone -> nothing is emphasised
one card highlighted -> the area being talked about

patterns.name: Bands of tiles with a side label
patterns.structure: Horizontal bands, each named in a narrow block at the left, each holding a row of tiles; the last band is one full-width statement.
content_fit: a portfolio read on two axes at once - areas across, layers down
what a company offers, in what shapes, on what basis
the closing band is the sentence that ties the whole picture together

bands.note: at 14pt four bands leave the tiles too short to hold a line

variants: no sub-tiles -> a plainer grid
drop the side labels -> stacked rows

patterns.name: Claim, figures and a picture area
patterns.structure: A three-line claim top left, a row of figure blocks under it, and a picture area filling the right half.
content_fit: who we are and the numbers that prove it
the picture area takes a map, a photo or a diagram - whatever the claim needs
three figures is the point: more and none of them registers
variants: picture on the left -> mirrored
no picture -> the claim and figures fill the slide

patterns.name: Four blocks in a loop
patterns.structure: Four offset blocks, each with a large figure behind its heading and a short list; the offset carries the loop.
content_fit: four areas that belong to one cycle rather than a straight sequence
the loop says it comes back round - use a chevron row when it does not
each block takes a heading and about three lines
variants: straight row instead of offset -> a plainer read
a connecting line around them -> emphasises the cycle, but that is a brand call
patterns.carrier: the offset that carries the order

patterns.name: Case study with a fact card
patterns.structure: A heading, a lead paragraph and running text on the left; a card on the right holding four labelled facts.
content_fit: one customer, one project, one story - with the hard facts beside it
the facts are what a reader scans first: who, what field, where, how big
works for a profile of a person or a place just as well
variants: facts as a row under the text -> a wider story column
add a picture area above the fact card

patterns.name: Wall of quotes
patterns.structure: Three offset cards, each with a quote mark, the quotation, and a round avatar area with a name and a role.
content_fit: what other people say - customers, staff, partners
the avatar area stays a grey circle until a real picture goes in
three is the number that reads as a wall without becoming a list
variants: no offset -> a plain row
one wide quote -> a single testimonial

patterns.name: Picture area with a numbered legend
patterns.structure: A large picture area on one side and a numbered list beside it, one line per entry.
content_fit: anything where a picture carries markers that need naming
a map with locations, a diagram with parts, a screenshot with callouts
the numbers tie the list to what is in the picture
variants: legend on the left -> mirrored
legend under the picture -> a wider picture area

patterns.name: Options as columns, criteria as rows
patterns.structure: A column per option with a head and a foot band, a criterion label per row, and one cell per crossing.
content_fit: several options measured on the same criteria
packages, tiers, vendors, variants - the head names them, the foot closes them
cells hold a mark, a number or two words, never a sentence
variants: drop the foot band -> a plain matrix
one column in a darker tone -> the recommended option

patterns.name: Bars growing away from a shared centre
patterns.structure: A centre column of labels with bars running left and right from it, one pair per row, and a head band over each side.
content_fit: two things measured on the same scale, row by row
two years, two products, two regions - the mirror makes the difference visible
the centre column holds the category, never a value
variants: values printed at the bar ends
one side shaded lighter -> the reference

patterns.name: Two blocks of figures and a total
patterns.structure: Two headed blocks of label-and-value rows side by side, with a full-width block under them carrying the result.
content_fit: a calculation shown as its parts and its outcome
inputs and steps above, the answer below - a cost model, a budget, a forecast
the value column stays narrow: figures, never sentences
variants: one block only -> a wider table
the total block in a lighter tone -> less emphasis on the outcome

patterns.name: Grid of tiles with a picture area
patterns.structure: A grid of equal tiles, each holding a picture area and a caption under it.
content_fit: a portfolio, a product range, a set of services - things that are equal in rank
the picture area takes an icon, a photo or a screenshot
the caption is a name, not a sentence
variants: one tone for all tiles -> nothing is emphasised
no picture area -> a grid of named blocks

patterns.name: Wall of logo areas
patterns.structure: An even grid of equal areas, each holding one logo.
content_fit: partners, customers, tools, certifications - a wall that says how many
the areas stay equal so no logo outranks another, whatever its shape
nothing but logos: a caption per logo turns this into a tile grid
variants: fewer, larger areas -> a handful of key partners
one row only -> a strip under other content

patterns.name: List on the left, one thing spelled out on the right
patterns.structure: A list of points on the left, and a panel on the right holding a stack of graded levels.
content_fit: the points of an offer, with one of them broken open beside it
the panel takes anything ordered - levels, tiers, steps, sizes
the left list is prose, the right panel is labels
variants: panel on the left -> mirrored
levels as equal tones -> nothing is ranked

patterns.name: Title slide
patterns.structure: A kicker, a two-line title, a subtitle and a footer line on the left; a full-height picture area on the right.
content_fit: the first slide of a deck
the footer line takes the date, the occasion or the audience
the picture area is where a brand puts its shape, photo or gradient
variants: no picture area -> the title fills the width
picture on the left -> mirrored

patterns.name: Agenda with numbers
patterns.structure: A heading and a line of context on the left; a numbered list of chapters on the right.
content_fit: the agenda of a deck, or a summary of what was covered
chapter names, never sentences
the same shape works as a table of contents for a document
variants: numbers as filled circles instead of plain figures
one chapter marked -> shows where in the deck you are

patterns.name: Section divider
patterns.structure: A large chapter number, the chapter name and one line of what is coming; a picture area beside it.
content_fit: the break between two parts of a deck
the line under the rule says what the section covers, in one sentence
the number ties it back to the agenda
variants: no picture area -> a quiet text divider
the whole slide in a dark tone -> a harder break

patterns.name: Closing slide with contact details
patterns.structure: A two-line closing statement, a code area, and labelled contact lines beside it; a picture area on the right.
content_fit: the last slide of a deck
the code area takes a QR code, a link block or nothing
three contact lines is enough: who, how, where
variants: no code area -> more room for contact lines
centred on the whole slide -> a plain thank-you

patterns.name: Person profile
patterns.structure: A portrait area on the left; a name, a role and four labelled facts on the right.
content_fit: one person: a speaker, an expert, a contact, a new colleague
the four facts are what matters about them here - experience, field, focus, proof
works for a place or an organisation just as well
variants: portrait as a circle -> softer, but that is a brand call
two people side by side -> half the facts each

patterns.name: Row of people
patterns.structure: Equal columns, each a portrait area with a name, a role and a line under it.
content_fit: the people on a project, a team, a panel, a board
four is the most that keeps the portraits large enough to recognise
the line under the role is one sentence, not a biography
variants: portraits as circles -> a brand call
no description -> a tighter row of six

patterns.name: Table, findings, and the sentence underneath
patterns.structure: A data table on the left with one row marked, a panel of short findings on the right, and a full-width band under both.
content_fit: a comparison where one row is us, or one row is the point
the findings are the reading, the band is the conclusion
the band is what stops a table from being handed over uninterpreted
variants: no marked row -> a neutral comparison
findings under the table -> a wider table

patterns.name: Chart, findings, and the sentence underneath
patterns.structure: A live chart on the left, two finding panels on the right, and a full-width band under both.
content_fit: a development over time with what it means beside it
the panels name the two things worth taking away, the band the conclusion
a line chart for a trend, a column chart for a comparison
variants: findings under the chart -> a wider chart
no band -> the chart has to speak for itself

patterns.name: Label and value blocks
patterns.structure: A grid of blocks, each split into a dark label part and a lighter value part.
content_fit: a fact sheet: project, owner, budget, deadline, scope, risk
the label is one or two words, the value a short line
reads faster than a table because each pair stands on its own
variants: one column -> a list of facts
all blocks one tone -> nothing is grouped

patterns.name: Claim beside a group of tiles
patterns.structure: A claim in a panel on the left, a group of tiles on the right, each tile one surface carrying a marker, a heading and a line of text, and a tab over the group naming it.
content_fit: one sentence that holds for everything in the group
a range of services, all of which share a property
the tab is the group's name, the panel is why it matters
variants: claim on the right -> mirrored
no tab -> a plainer group
marker and heading only -> six tiles instead of four
no marker -> the heading starts at the tile's edge

patterns.name: Cycle with numbered stages
patterns.structure: A ring around a named centre, with numbered markers on it and a label to the left and right of each.
content_fit: stages that come back round - a customer journey, a review cycle, a season
the centre names what the cycle is about
not for a sequence with an end: that is a path or a chevron row
variants: labels only on one side -> a legend layout
no ring, just the markers -> a lighter read

patterns.name: One claim, the things that carry it
patterns.structure: A statement box on top, a stem and a cross bar, and a row of boxes hanging from it.
content_fit: a conclusion and what it rests on
a goal and the measures under it, a decision and its reasons
the top box states it, the lower boxes are why it holds
variants: two levels of boxes -> a small org chart
the top box in a light tone -> a question rather than a claim

patterns.name: Grouped measures with priority and owner
patterns.structure: A legend of priority marks, then grouped bands: a group name on the left, and per row a priority mark, the measure, and the owner on the right.
content_fit: a plan: what is to be done, how urgent, and by whom
the grouping is the theme, the mark is the priority, the right column is the team
one line per measure - a measure that needs two lines is two measures
variants: no groups -> a flat list of measures
a date column instead of the owner
drop the legend -> the marks have to be self-explaining

patterns.name: Points with a heading each
patterns.structure: A marker, a short heading and a line or two of text, repeated down the slide.
content_fit: the plainest way to make several points on one slide
each point gets a name and an explanation - if a point needs neither, use a plain list
the slide most decks are mostly made of

points.note: at 14pt six points leave one line of text each

variants: no headings -> a plain bullet list with more room per point
two columns -> up to ten shorter points
numbers instead of markers -> an ordered list

patterns.name: Points in two columns
patterns.structure: The same point-with-heading shape, in two columns, read down the left first.
content_fit: eight points that belong together and do not fit in one column
two groups of four, if the columns are given headings
reading order is down then across - say so if it should be across then down
variants: column headings -> two named groups
one column -> more room per point

patterns.name: Title and a plain table
patterns.structure: A headed table filling the content area, first column text and the rest values.
content_fit: figures that belong in rows and columns and need no picture
a price list, a schedule, a set of measurements
when a table needs a reading beside it, use the table-with-findings pattern
variants: no banding -> rules between the rows instead
a total row in a darker tone at the bottom

patterns.name: One picture, full width
patterns.structure: A picture area filling nearly the whole slide, with a caption and a source line under it.
content_fit: a screenshot, a photograph, a diagram made elsewhere
the caption says what to look at, not what it is
the right-hand line takes the source or the date
variants: caption over the picture -> a fuller bleed
two pictures side by side -> a comparison

patterns.name: Title, intro and a free area
patterns.structure: A title, one intro paragraph, and the whole content area left open.
content_fit: the fallback when nothing else fits: a screenshot, a pasted chart, a drawing
the free area is the content area every other pattern divides up
use it knowingly, not because the library was not searched
variants: without the intro -> the free area grows by 0.75in
the area split in two -> a rough two-column layout

patterns.name: A question and the answers to it
patterns.structure: A question across the full width, and the answers as equal cards under it.
content_fit: a slide that opens a discussion rather than closing one
an objection and the responses, a decision and the options
the question must be a real question, not a heading with a question mark
variants: one answer -> a statement slide
answers as a numbered list -> a ranking rather than options

patterns.name: Offer: two blocks, results, terms
patterns.structure: A kicker, title and coloured subtitle; two blocks side by side, each a heading, a paragraph and bullet lines; a result row under them; a dark band of labelled terms at the foot.
content_fit: one offer on one slide: the situation, what happens, what comes out, what it costs
the left block is where the customer is, the right is what you do
the terms band takes duration, place, price - the three things asked next

bullets_per_block.note: at 14pt four bullets need the result row dropped

variants: no terms band -> an offer without a price
results as a row of cards -> more room per result

patterns.name: Phases with headings above the line
patterns.structure: A kicker, title and subtitle; phase headings above a horizontal line, a marker on it per phase, and the text below; a footnote at the foot.
content_fit: a sequence where every step needs two or three sentences, not a label
before, during, after and the outcome - the last marker sits darker
the footnote takes the conditions that hold for all phases
variants: markers as numbers -> a strictly counted sequence
no line -> four columns of text under headings
patterns.carrier: the line the phases sit on

patterns.name: Numbered sections stacked
patterns.structure: Full-width bands stacked down the slide, each with a large number on the left, a heading and a short list.
content_fit: three areas that each need several lines - a quarterly review, a status report
the number is an anchor, not a ranking
the shape a written summary takes when it has to go on one slide
variants: nested lines under a bullet -> a deeper breakdown
one section in a darker tone -> the one that matters

patterns.name: Picture area with a feature grid
patterns.structure: A picture area on one side; on the other a grid of pairs, each an icon area, a heading and a paragraph.
content_fit: a product or a screen with the four things worth saying about it
the icon area stays a grey square until a real icon goes in
four pairs is the balance point: six make the text too short to say anything
variants: picture on the right -> mirrored
one column of features -> a taller picture area
no icon areas -> a plain text grid
